passage: At the community centre's after-school room, the rain had made every parent late. Five-year-old Yash had not eaten since lunch. He whined at the puzzle, kicked the table leg, then smacked his older brother Chaitanya for touching his crayons. When Chaitanya offered him half a biscuit, it snapped in two, and Yash burst into loud tears. "He's not usually like this," Chaitanya told the helper, Mrs Kamath. She didn't lecture. She fetched a banana and some crackers from the snack tin and sat Yash on a beanbag. Soon he was giggling and sharing his crayons.

qa.q: What happened to the biscuit Chaitanya offered?
Why did Yash burst into tears over the biscuit?
qa.a: He was very hungry, so he felt cross and overwhelmed, and a small upset felt huge.

qa.q: Why did Mrs Kamath's response work?
qa.a: She gave food and a quiet seat instead of a lecture, meeting the physical need behind the mood.

qa.q: What was the afternoon like for Chaitanya?
qa.a: Chaitanya got smacked and cried at while trying to help, yet still understood this was not how Yash usually is.

grounding: Shows a young child late for food turning whiny, hitting a sibling and crying over a broken biscuit, and a snack restoring him better than a lecture.

passage: From my balcony I, Bhavna, can see into the Mehtas' courtyard. On Tuesday their dinner ran late; Mrs Mehta was stuck on a work call. Little Deepak, five, went from singing to whining. He yanked his sister's plait, and when she yelled, he threw himself on the steps, wailing that his biscuit had broken "all wrong". Mrs Mehta began a lecture about manners, stopped, and handed him a chapati roll. Soon he was waving up at me. "Bhavna didi, look at my car!" I can't know what was in his head, but the change was hard to miss.

qa.q: Why did dinner run late on Tuesday?
qa.a: Mrs Mehta was stuck on a work call.

qa.q: What might Deepak have been feeling when he threw himself on the steps?
qa.a: He was probably hungry and miserable, so a broken biscuit felt like a disaster.

qa.q: What was wiser than the lecture, and why?
qa.a: Handing him a chapati roll; the mood came from hunger, so food settled him faster than words about manners.

qa.q: How might Deepak's sister see the evening?
qa.a: She had her plait yanked for no reason and may have felt hurt and angry, without knowing he was hungry.

grounding: Illustrates a young child whose late dinner turns him whiny and rough with a sibling, and food restoring him better than a lecture.
